formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the BOB allowance the owner gives the spender to exactly `value`, replacing any earlier allowance (ERC20Permit.permit -> _approve(_holder, _spender, _value)).
The signature works until `deadline` and uses up the owner's current nonce (_checkPermit: block.timestamp <= _deadline; nonces[_holder]++).
If the spender submits the same signature itself through receiveWithPermit, `value` BOB moves straight from the owner to the spender, and the allowance ends at 0 (ERC20Permit.receiveWithPermit).
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens". The fields show the spender address in raw form, the max spending amount in BOB ("Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), the valid-until date and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit has no interpolatedIntent, so the intent line leaves out the amount, token and spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json display.formats Permit: intent "Authorize spending of tokens", and there is no interpolatedIntent. The fields value (tokenAmount) and spender carry this information.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Allow {spender} to spend up to {value} until {deadline}". Give spender the addressName format so the sentence reads well.

findings.title: The same Permit signature can also be redeemed with receiveWithPermit, which moves the tokens to the spender at once.
findings.evidence: ERC20Permit.sol receiveWithPermit: _checkPermit(_holder, msg.sender, _value, ...); _approve(_holder, msg.sender, 0); _transfer(_holder, msg.sender, _value). This uses the same PERMIT_TYPEHASH that is signed here.
findings.fix: No descriptor change is required, because the result matches an approval followed by transferFrom of up to `value`. A label such as "Max amount spender can take" would make this clearer.
